bodyWidth.doc: Overall width of the bus, without mirrors.
bodyWidth.source: Maximum width of road vehicles in the EU (Directive 96/53/EC)

bodyHeight.doc: Height of the bus from the road to the roof.

rearOverhang.doc: Distance from the rear axle to the back of the bus; the rear axle is the reference point of the bus.

wheelbase.doc: Distance between the front and the rear axle; sets the turning radius.

frontDoorSetback.doc: Distance from the front of the bus to the middle of the front door, which must face the stop.

steeringRatio.doc: Steering wheel turn per front wheel turn (cabin view).

texturePixelsPerMetre.doc: Pixel density of the bus pixel-art textures.

bodyLength.doc: Articulated bus: length of the front body, up to the bellows (front overhang 2.8 m + wheelbase + rearOverhang).
bodyLength.source: Mercedes-Benz Citaro G (18.1 m) data sheet, rounded: overhangs 2.8 and 3.5 m, wheelbases 5.85 and 5.99 m

wheelbase.doc: Articulated bus: distance between the front and the middle axle; the middle axle is the reference point of the bus.
wheelbase.source: Mercedes-Benz Citaro G (18.1 m) data sheet, rounded: overhangs 2.8 and 3.5 m, wheelbases 5.85 and 5.99 m

rearOverhang.doc: Articulated bus: distance from the middle axle to the back of the front body (hitchOffset minus half the bellows).

hitchOffset.doc: Articulated bus: distance from the middle axle back to the joint between the two bodies.

bellowsLength.doc: Articulated bus: length of the bellows, centred on the joint.

trailerWheelbase.doc: Articulated bus: distance from the joint to the rear axle (middle-to-rear wheelbase minus hitchOffset).
trailerWheelbase.source: Mercedes-Benz Citaro G (18.1 m) data sheet, rounded: overhangs 2.8 and 3.5 m, wheelbases 5.85 and 5.99 m

trailerRearOverhang.doc: Articulated bus: distance from the rear axle to the back of the bus; the whole bus is 18.1 m long.
trailerRearOverhang.source: Mercedes-Benz Citaro G (18.1 m) data sheet, rounded: overhangs 2.8 and 3.5 m, wheelbases 5.85 and 5.99 m

maxArticulation.doc: Articulated bus: largest angle between the two bodies (about 49°); the joint stops the rear body beyond it.

maxSpeed.source: French urban speed limit (Code de la route, art. R413-3)

acceleration.doc: Forward acceleration from standstill; it falls to zero at the top speed. Firmer than a real city bus (about 1.2 m/s²) so that the game feels responsive.

reverseAcceleration.doc: Acceleration in reverse (brake key held at standstill).

brakingStart.doc: Deceleration as soon as the brake key is pressed; it grows up to `braking` while the key is held.

braking.doc: Largest deceleration of the service brake, reached after `brakeRampTime` with the brake key held.
braking.source: Emergency braking of a city bus, about 6 m/s² (UNECE Regulation 13, category M3: at least 5 m/s²)

brakeRampTime.doc: Time the brake key must be held to go from `brakingStart` to `braking`; releasing the key starts again from `brakingStart`.

rollingDeceleration.doc: Deceleration when coasting (no key pressed), before air drag.

airDrag.doc: Coasting deceleration added per square of speed (deceleration = airDrag × v²).

slopeFactor.doc: Share of the gravity along the slope felt by the bus; below 1 to keep hills drivable.

maxSteer.doc: Largest front wheel angle at low speed: with the 6 m wheelbase, the outer front corner sweeps a circle of about 10.8 m radius.
maxSteer.source: Turning circle of a 12 m city bus, about 21 to 22 m between walls (e.g. Mercedes-Benz Citaro data sheet)

steerReductionAtMaxSpeed.doc: Share of the largest wheel angle removed at top speed (linear in speed).

steerRate.doc: Speed at which the wheels turn while a steering key is held.

steerReturnRate.doc: Speed at which the wheels come back to centre once the steering keys are released.

bumpRebound.doc: Share of the speed kept, backwards, after hitting a building.

bumpCooldown.doc: Shortest time between two reported collisions.

stepsPerSecond.doc: Fixed rate of the driving and service simulation, independent of the display rate.

laneOffset.doc: Distance to the right of the route centre line where the bus starts, where the autopilot drives and where the guidance is drawn; less where the street is too narrow (see kerbMargin).

kerbMargin.doc: Smallest gap between the side of the bus and the kerb in its lane: in narrow and one-way streets the lane moves towards the route centre line to keep it.

stopDistance.doc: Largest distance between the front door and the stop for the stop to be served. Middle choice of the player (default); presets.difficulty holds the others.

stopSpeed.doc: The bus must be slower than this for the doors to open.

doorTime.doc: Time the doors must stay open with the front door at a stop to serve it.

doorMoveTime.doc: Time the doors take to open or to close; the bus is held still until they are closed.

alightProbability.doc: Chance that someone on board asks to get off at a stop (stop requested).

boardProbability.doc: Chance that people wait at a stop.

missedStopDistance.doc: A stop the bus passes by more than this distance along the route is missed.

offRouteDistance.doc: Distance from the route beyond which the bus is off route. Middle choice of the player (default); presets.difficulty holds the others.

offRouteDelay.doc: Time off route before the warning shows.

onTimeTolerance.doc: A stop served within this delay of its timetable is on time; the SAE colours larger delays. Middle choice of the player (default); presets.difficulty holds the others.

saeDeltaThreshold.doc: The SAE shows the delay or advance once it exceeds this value, else 'on time'.

distance.doc: HD-2D view: distance from the camera to its target.

pitch.doc: HD-2D view: angle of the camera above the horizon.

fov.doc: HD-2D view: vertical field of view.

ahead.doc: HD-2D view: the target is this far in front of the bus centre.

followTime.doc: HD-2D view: time constant of the camera turning after the bus heading.

focus.doc: HD-2D view: height of the sharp band of the tilt-shift blur, from the bottom of the screen.

blur.doc: HD-2D view: largest tilt-shift blur radius, in internal pixels.

distance.doc: Chase view: distance from the camera to its target.

pitch.doc: Chase view: angle of the camera above the horizon.

fov.doc: Chase view: vertical field of view.

ahead.doc: Chase view: the target is this far in front of the bus centre.

followTime.doc: Chase view: time constant of the camera turning after the bus heading.

focus.doc: Chase view: height of the sharp band of the tilt-shift blur, from the bottom of the screen.

blur.doc: Chase view: largest tilt-shift blur radius, in internal pixels.

distance.doc: Sky view: distance from the camera to its target.

pitch.doc: Sky view: angle of the camera above the horizon.

fov.doc: Sky view: vertical field of view.

ahead.doc: Sky view: the target is this far in front of the bus centre.

followTime.doc: Sky view: time constant of the camera turning after the bus heading.

focus.doc: Sky view: height of the sharp band of the tilt-shift blur, from the bottom of the screen.

blur.doc: Sky view: largest tilt-shift blur radius, in internal pixels.

eyeFromFront.doc: Cabin view: distance of the eye behind the front of the bus.

eyeHeight.doc: Cabin view: height of the eye above the road.

eyeSide.doc: Cabin view: side offset of the eye from the middle of the bus (negative = left).

pitch.doc: Cabin view: angle of the view below the horizon.

fov.doc: Cabin view: vertical field of view.

eyeFromFront.doc: Passenger view: distance of the eye behind the front of the bus.

eyeHeight.doc: Passenger view: height of the eye above the road.

eyeSide.doc: Passenger view: side offset of the eye from the middle of the bus (negative = left).

pitch.doc: Passenger view: angle of the view below the horizon.

fov.doc: Passenger view: vertical field of view.

lines.doc: Mirrors: height of their internal image (HD-2D pixels).

top.doc: Mirrors: top edge, from the top of the screen.

height.doc: Mirrors: height of the mirror heads above the road.

outward.doc: Mirrors: the view aims this far outwards 10 m behind the mirror, to show the side of the road.

interiorNear.doc: Near clipping distance in the views from inside the bus (1 m outside).

targetHeight.doc: Height of the camera target above the road.

groundClearance.doc: The camera never goes lower than this above the ground under it.

zoomMin.doc: Closest mouse wheel zoom, as a share of the view distance.

zoomMax.doc: Farthest mouse wheel zoom, as a multiple of the view distance.

zoomPerWheelUnit.doc: Zoom speed: the distance is multiplied by exp(zoomPerWheelUnit × wheel delta).

yawPerPixel.doc: Free camera: turn around the bus per pixel of horizontal mouse drag.

pitchPerPixel.doc: Free camera: change of pitch per pixel of vertical mouse drag.

pitchMin.doc: Free camera: lowest pitch, kept above the horizon.

pitchMax.doc: Free camera: highest pitch, kept short of straight down.

returnTime.doc: Free camera: time constant of the return to the automatic view.

returnDone.doc: Free camera: the return is complete below this angle.

internalLines.doc: Height of the internal image; it is scaled up to the screen with visible pixels (HD-2D look). Middle choice of the player (default); presets.quality holds the others.

tiltShiftBand.doc: Half height of the sharp band of the tilt-shift blur.

viewDistance.doc: Farthest distance drawn; the sky dome sits just inside it. Middle choice of the player (default); presets.viewDistance holds the others.

fogFar.doc: Distance where the fog hides everything. Middle choice of the player (default); presets.viewDistance holds the others.

shadowMapSize.doc: Resolution of the shadow map. Middle choice of the player (default); presets.quality holds the others.

shadowRadius.doc: Half side of the square around the bus where shadows are drawn.

elevation.doc: Day: sun elevation of this key moment; the look is blended between the two nearest moments.

skyTop.doc: Day: colour of the sky at the zenith.

skyMiddle.doc: Day: colour of the sky halfway up.

horizon.doc: Day: colour of the fog and of the sky at the horizon.

ambientSky.doc: Day: ambient light coming from the sky.

ambientGround.doc: Day: ambient light bounced by the ground.

ambientIntensity.doc: Day: intensity of the ambient light.

night.doc: Day: how much the street lights, windows and vehicle lights shine (0 off, 1 full).

skyTop.doc: Low sun: colour of the sky at the zenith.

skyMiddle.doc: Low sun: colour of the sky halfway up.

horizon.doc: Low sun: colour of the fog and of the sky at the horizon.

light.doc: Low sun: colour of the sunlight.

lightIntensity.doc: Low sun: intensity of the sunlight.

ambientSky.doc: Low sun: ambient light coming from the sky.

ambientGround.doc: Low sun: ambient light bounced by the ground.

ambientIntensity.doc: Low sun: intensity of the ambient light.

night.doc: Low sun: how much the street lights, windows and vehicle lights shine (0 off, 1 full).

skyTop.doc: Sunset: colour of the sky at the zenith.

skyMiddle.doc: Sunset: colour of the sky halfway up.

horizon.doc: Sunset: colour of the fog and of the sky at the horizon.

ambientSky.doc: Sunset: ambient light coming from the sky.

ambientGround.doc: Sunset: ambient light bounced by the ground.

ambientIntensity.doc: Sunset: intensity of the ambient light.

night.doc: Sunset: how much the street lights, windows and vehicle lights shine (0 off, 1 full).

elevation.doc: Dusk (end of civil twilight at -6°): sun elevation of this key moment; the look is blended between the two nearest moments.

skyTop.doc: Dusk (end of civil twilight at -6°): colour of the sky at the zenith.

skyMiddle.doc: Dusk (end of civil twilight at -6°): colour of the sky halfway up.

horizon.doc: Dusk (end of civil twilight at -6°): colour of the fog and of the sky at the horizon.

light.doc: Dusk (end of civil twilight at -6°): colour of the sunlight.

lightIntensity.doc: Dusk (end of civil twilight at -6°): intensity of the sunlight.

ambientSky.doc: Dusk (end of civil twilight at -6°): ambient light coming from the sky.

ambientGround.doc: Dusk (end of civil twilight at -6°): ambient light bounced by the ground.

ambientIntensity.doc: Dusk (end of civil twilight at -6°): intensity of the ambient light.

night.doc: Dusk (end of civil twilight at -6°): how much the street lights, windows and vehicle lights shine (0 off, 1 full).

elevation.doc: Night: sun elevation of this key moment; the look is blended between the two nearest moments.

skyTop.doc: Night: colour of the sky at the zenith.

skyMiddle.doc: Night: colour of the sky halfway up.

horizon.doc: Night: colour of the fog and of the sky at the horizon.

ambientSky.doc: Night: ambient light coming from the sky.

ambientGround.doc: Night: ambient light bounced by the ground.

ambientIntensity.doc: Night: intensity of the ambient light.

night.doc: Night: how much the street lights, windows and vehicle lights shine (0 off, 1 full).

moonIntensity.doc: Intensity of the light of a full moon high in the sky; it fades with the lit fraction and near the horizon.

minLightElevation.doc: The sun or moon light comes from at least this high, so that shadows stay short at sunrise and sunset.

lampSpacing.doc: Distance between two street lights along a kerb (Grenoble streets: about 25 to 40 m).

lampGlowSize.doc: Size of the glowing halo of a street light at night.

lampColor.doc: Colour of the street lights (sodium-like warm white).

realLights.doc: Street lights nearest to the bus that really light the scene at night; the others only glow.

realLightIntensity.doc: Intensity of each real street light at night.

realLightDistance.doc: Reach of a real street light.

realLightFade.doc: A real street light fades out over this distance from the bus, so that it does not pop when it moves to a nearer lamp.

windowShare.doc: Share of the windows lit at night.

windowGlow.doc: Brightness of the lit windows at night.

vehicleLightGlow.doc: Brightness of the head, tail and destination lights of the buses at night.

brakeLightGlow.doc: Brightness of the brake lights of the player's bus while braking, day and night.

headlightIntensity.doc: Intensity of the headlights of the player's bus at night.

day.doc: Winter (mid-January): day of the year of this key moment; the landscape is blended between the two nearest moments, across the new year.

land.doc: Winter (mid-January): colour of the plain ground of the city.

park.doc: Winter (mid-January): colour of the parks and lawns.

forest.doc: Winter (mid-January): colour of the woods of the city map.

lowland.doc: Winter (mid-January): colour of the valley floor around the city.

mountainForest.doc: Winter (mid-January): colour of the forests of the mountains.

leafDark.doc: Winter (mid-January): dark foliage of the street trees.

leafMiddle.doc: Winter (mid-January): middle foliage of the street trees.

leafLight.doc: Winter (mid-January): light foliage of the street trees.

leaves.doc: Winter (mid-January): how leafy the street trees are (0 bare branches, 1 full).

snowLine.doc: Winter (mid-January): altitude above which the mountains are white with snow.

day.doc: Spring (mid-April): day of the year of this key moment; the landscape is blended between the two nearest moments, across the new year.

land.doc: Spring (mid-April): colour of the plain ground of the city.

park.doc: Spring (mid-April): colour of the parks and lawns.

forest.doc: Spring (mid-April): colour of the woods of the city map.

lowland.doc: Spring (mid-April): colour of the valley floor around the city.

mountainForest.doc: Spring (mid-April): colour of the forests of the mountains.

leafDark.doc: Spring (mid-April): dark foliage of the street trees.

leafMiddle.doc: Spring (mid-April): middle foliage of the street trees.

leafLight.doc: Spring (mid-April): light foliage of the street trees.

leaves.doc: Spring (mid-April): how leafy the street trees are (0 bare branches, 1 full).

snowLine.doc: Spring (mid-April): altitude above which the mountains are white with snow.

land.doc: Summer (mid-July): colour of the plain ground of the city.

park.doc: Summer (mid-July): colour of the parks and lawns.

forest.doc: Summer (mid-July): colour of the woods of the city map.

lowland.doc: Summer (mid-July): colour of the valley floor around the city.

mountainForest.doc: Summer (mid-July): colour of the forests of the mountains.

leafDark.doc: Summer (mid-July): dark foliage of the street trees.

leafMiddle.doc: Summer (mid-July): middle foliage of the street trees.

leafLight.doc: Summer (mid-July): light foliage of the street trees.

leaves.doc: Summer (mid-July): how leafy the street trees are (0 bare branches, 1 full).

snowLine.doc: Summer (mid-July): altitude above which the mountains are white with snow.

day.doc: Autumn (late October): day of the year of this key moment; the landscape is blended between the two nearest moments, across the new year.

land.doc: Autumn (late October): colour of the plain ground of the city.

park.doc: Autumn (late October): colour of the parks and lawns.

forest.doc: Autumn (late October): colour of the woods of the city map.

lowland.doc: Autumn (late October): colour of the valley floor around the city.

mountainForest.doc: Autumn (late October): colour of the forests of the mountains.

leafDark.doc: Autumn (late October): dark foliage of the street trees.

leafMiddle.doc: Autumn (late October): middle foliage of the street trees.

leafLight.doc: Autumn (late October): light foliage of the street trees.

leaves.doc: Autumn (late October): how leafy the street trees are (0 bare branches, 1 full).

snowLine.doc: Autumn (late October): altitude above which the mountains are white with snow.

forestFrom.doc: Altitude where the forests of the mountains start.

forestBlend.doc: Height over which the valley floor turns into forest.

treeLine.doc: Altitude where the forests give way to rock (Northern Alps: about 1 800 m for the last trees, lower for dense forest).

rockFrom.doc: Altitude above which the mountains are bare rock.

rockColor.doc: Colour of the rock of the mountains.

snowFade.doc: Height over which the snow cover goes from none to full.

snowEdge.doc: The snow line moves up and down by up to this much from place to place.

snowOnForest.doc: Share of white on a snowy forest (the trees stay partly dark).

roadLift.doc: Height of the road mesh above the shaped ground; road pieces are coplanar with the ground (tools/streets.py), the lift only avoids depth fighting.

kerbHeight.doc: Height of the sidewalks above the ground: a low kerb, readable at the HD-2D resolution.

markingLift.doc: Height of the road markings above the road.

markingWidth.doc: Width of the centre lines, wider than real ones to stay visible at the HD-2D resolution.

dashLength.doc: Length of a dash of the centre lines.

dashGap.doc: Gap between two dashes of the centre lines.

deckCatch.doc: A bus closer than this to a bridge deck height drives on the deck; farther below, it drives under it.

deckMargin.doc: The water does not stop a bus this far beyond the sides and ends of a bridge deck: OSM decks are as narrow as the carriageway, the banks are skewed at the bridge ends, and the bus drifts in its lane (3 m lets the autopilot cross both bridges of the route).

kerbSearch.doc: A stop looks for the kerb up to this distance to the right of the route centre line (the widest street of the route puts it 7.3 m away, at Verdun – Préfecture); farther, it keeps its GTFS position.

shelterSetback.doc: Distance from the kerb to the middle of the shelter: its 2 m deep roof then stays above the 2.5 m sidewalk and clear of a bus at the kerb.

deepColor.doc: Colour of the water seen from above, before the sky reflection.

foamColor.doc: Colour of the foam along the banks.

quayColor.doc: Colour of the stone quay walls along the banks.

pixelSize.doc: Size of the pixels of the ripple and foam pattern, fixed in the world.

rippleSpeed.doc: Speed of the ripple animation (0 freezes it).

foamWidth.doc: Width of the foam band along the banks.

wallDepth.doc: Depth of the quay walls below the water surface.

stressSpacing.doc: Distance between the places along the route where the dummy vehicles of the performance test may appear.

stressSpeed.doc: Speed of the dummy vehicles of the performance test (?debug&stress=N), along the route in both directions.

turboMaxSpeed.doc: Debug mode: top speed with the turbo (Shift held).

turboFactor.doc: Debug mode: acceleration and braking multiplier of the turbo.

flySpeed.doc: Debug mode: speed of the free-flying camera.

flyFastFactor.doc: Debug mode: speed multiplier of the free-flying camera with Shift held.

flyMinHeight.doc: Debug mode: the free-flying camera stays this high above the ground.

timeStep.doc: Debug mode: the light jumps this much forward or back in time with the time keys.

initialMax.doc: Most people on board at the start of a service.

alightMax.doc: Most people getting off at a requested stop.

boardMax.doc: Most people waiting at a stop.

interval.doc: Time between two people getting off or on.

walkSpeed.source: Usual walking speed of adults (about 1.3 m/s)

walkAway.doc: How far people walk away from the bus after getting off.

looks.doc: Number of different people drawn (clothes, skin and hair picked per look).

dwellTime.doc: Time the other buses of the line stand at each stop, doors open.

maxDwellShare.doc: The dwell never takes more than this share of the scheduled time to the next stop.

catchUpSpeed.doc: Fastest progress of a late bus catching up with its timetable (50 km/h).

gap.doc: Distance a bus keeps behind the player's bus or the bus ahead of it when it has to wait.

laneTolerance.doc: The player's bus blocks a direction when its centre is within this distance of that route.

headingTolerance.doc: The player's bus blocks a direction only when it heads the same way as that route, within this angle.

searchWindow.doc: The player's bus is looked for along each route within this distance of where it was last found.

loadRadius.doc: The detailed layers of a tile (10 m ground, streets, trees, buildings) are built when the bus comes this close to the tile; the buildings are drawn as long as they are built.

unloadRadius.doc: The detailed layers of a tile are freed when the bus is farther than this (beyond loadRadius, so that driving along the limit does not build and free them in turn).

fineGroundDistance.doc: The 10 m ground grid of a tile is drawn within this distance of the bus; farther, its light ground.

streetDistance.doc: Carriageways, sidewalks, kerbs and markings of a tile are drawn within this distance of the bus (farther, the ground texture shows the streets).

treeDistance.doc: The trees of a tile are drawn within this distance of the bus.

lightGroundStep.doc: The light ground of a far tile keeps one point out of this many of the 10 m grid (50 m cells): 25 times fewer triangles.

buildBudget.doc: Time spent building the tiles that come near, per frame (at least one tile), so that driving never stutters.

modelDistance.doc: Moving objects closer than this to the camera are drawn as 3D models.

spriteDistance.doc: Moving objects farther than modelDistance and closer than this are drawn as flat sprites; beyond, they are not drawn.

simulationRadius.doc: Moving objects closer than this to the player's bus are simulated every frame.

farUpdateInterval.doc: Farther than simulationRadius, a moving object is simulated once per interval, with the time saved up.

spawnMinDistance.doc: Ambient objects (traffic, pedestrians) never appear closer than this to the player's bus.

spawnRadius.doc: Ambient objects appear at most this far from the player's bus.

despawnRadius.doc: Ambient objects farther than this from the player's bus are removed (beyond spawnRadius, so that they do not flicker).

capacity.doc: Largest number of instances of one model drawn at once (size of the instance buffers).

internalLines.doc: Low graphics quality: height of the internal image (fewer pixels to draw).

shadowMapSize.doc: Low graphics quality: resolution of the shadow map.

internalLines.doc: High graphics quality: height of the internal image (finer pixels).

shadowMapSize.doc: High graphics quality: resolution of the shadow map.

fogFar.doc: Near view distance: distance where the fog hides everything (the mountains fade out).

viewDistance.doc: Near view distance: farthest distance drawn.

fogFar.doc: Medium view distance: distance where the fog hides everything.

viewDistance.doc: Medium view distance: farthest distance drawn.

stopDistance.doc: Easy: largest distance between the front door and the stop for the stop to be served.

onTimeTolerance.doc: Easy: a stop served within this delay of its timetable is on time.

offRouteDistance.doc: Easy: distance from the route beyond which the bus is off route.

stopDistance.doc: Hard: largest distance between the front door and the stop for the stop to be served.

onTimeTolerance.doc: Hard: a stop served within this delay of its timetable is on time.

offRouteDistance.doc: Hard: distance from the route beyond which the bus is off route.
